newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 25.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 25.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Wednesday
* On Tuesday, the Dow Jones industrial average ended up 153.80 points, or 2.02 percent, at 7,758.06 after Monday's 192-point drop as blue chips staged a powerful rebound.
* Senior Indonesian economist Sumitro Djojohadikusumo shares the World Bank's concern that economic reform in the country has lost momentum.
* On Tuesday, the Jakarta composite index closed down 6.25 points, or 0.87 percent, at 713.39 points after hitting an intra-day low of 711.42 points on profit-taking.
* On Wednesday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,431.75/32.75 at 0155 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,431.25/32.00.

* Noodle and snack-food maker PT Indofood on reports that it targeted a net profit of 508 billion rupiah for 1997. Also after it won shareholder approval to pay 1996 dividend of 47 rupiah per share and to increase authorised capital to three trillion rupiah from one trillion rupiah in anticipation of further expansion.

* Cement maker PT Indocement Tunggal Perkasa after its shareholders approved a 70 rupiah dividend for 1996. Also following media reports that it expected a net profit growth of 15 to 18 percent for 1997 and total sales of about seven trillion rupiah.
* Property firm PT Jakarta International Hotel Development (JIHD) on reports that it will increase its stake in cellular phone operator Satelindo to 25 percent from the current 21.37 percent.

* Retailer and information technology company PT Multipolar Corporation on reports that it will propose a rights issue to raise 754.2 billion rupiah which will be used to increase its equity to 940 billion rupiah from 186 billion rupiah.
* Engineering firm PT Bukaka Teknik Utama ahead of a shareholder meeting in the afternoon coupled with market talk of a possible higher dividend.
* Bakrie Land Development following reports that it would invest 130 billion rupiah to develop a 340-hectare integrated tourism and industrial area in Lampung, Sumatra.
